beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Society That Selects Us examines a paradox inside modern success.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A society can reward education while making family life harder to sustain.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This scientific and philosophical essay follows that tension through fertility, personality, and institutions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It separates genetic change from cultural transmission, social filtering, and demographic shifts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That separation helps readers examine selection without mistaking every social change for biological destiny.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapter four compares people who express the same wish for two children.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One has nearby grandparents, affordable housing, and a predictable working day.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The other faces expensive rent, repeated moves, and a long commute.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The difference lies between wanting a family and having room to realize it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book calls attention to compatibilities between personal traits and institutional arrangements.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those barriers become the starting point for the book's four possible futures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One scenario redraws the city around nearby housing, schools, work, and care.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A second child would no longer necessarily require another exhausting move.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed change supports family choices while preserving different professions and ways of living.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This metropolis of proximity is a scenario to examine, not a guaranteed forecast.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The wider comparison asks which freedoms each social arrangement preserves or puts under pressure.
